title: Einstein's 1923 paper saying general relativity fits with the ether

tellings.link_reason: Both are about Einstein's early-1920s paper bringing back the ether as compatible with general relativity.

tellings.page: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
tellings.quote: Recapitulating, we may say that according to the general theory of relativity space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether.

tellings.page: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
tellings.quote: According to the general theory of relativity space without ether is unthinkable; for in such space there not only would be no propagation of light, but also no possibility of existence for standards of space and time (measuring-rods and clocks), nor therefore any space-time intervals in the physical sense.

plain: The claim is that Einstein himself once said his general theory of relativity is compatible with the ether, the old idea of an invisible medium filling all of space that physics is usually said to have thrown out. Michels says it in his own words, placing the paper in 1923, and a Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents he links to UFO-like craft, makes the same point but dates it to 1921, adding that Einstein used the idea even though he had long been against it. The text they mean is Ether and the Theory of Relativity, an address Einstein gave at the University of Leiden on May 5, 1920, later printed in his book Sidelights on Relativity, so it is earlier than either date the tellers give. The address itself says plainly that "according to the general theory of relativity space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether," and even that "space without ether is unthinkable." It also says that "the special theory of relativity does not compel us to deny ether." So on the core claim the document backs the tellers quite directly. What it leaves to the reader is what kind of ether this is: Einstein warns it "may not be thought of" as made of parts that can be tracked through time, and that "the idea of motion may not be applied to it," so whether it is the same ether the guests have in mind is a step of reading the text does not settle. The point matters to them because, if Einstein left room for an ether, ideas about tapping the fabric of space are less fringe than they seem.

discussion.by: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
discussion.text: The text in Einstein's Sidelights on Relativity reads "An Address delivered on May 5th, 1920, in the University of Leyden", so the work the tellers mean dates from 1920, where the host says 1923 and Salvatore Pais 1921. In it Einstein says that "according to the general theory of relativity space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether", the claim the tellers give it.
